ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, a line $y = \frac{1}{2}x + b$ (where $b$ is a constant and $b < 2$) is drawn through point $P(0, 2)$ perpendicular to it, with the foot of the perpendicular at point $Q$. What is the value of $\sin\angle OPQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Given $\because \angle PBQ = \angle ABO$,\\
$PQ \perp AQ$, $BO \perp AO$\\
$\therefore \angle PBQ + \angle OPQ = \angle ABO + \angle OAB$\\
$= 90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle OPQ = \angle OAB$\\
From $y=\frac{1}{2}x+b$, setting $x=0$, $y=b$,\\
Setting $y=0$,\\
$x=-2b$\\
$\therefore AO=2b$, $BO=b$\\
In $\triangle AOB$ right,\\
$AB=\sqrt{AO^2 + BO^2} = \sqrt{5}b$\\
$\therefore \sin\angle OPQ =\sin\angle BAO =\frac{BO}{AB} =\frac{b}{\sqrt{5}b} = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, the line y = 1/2 x + b slants upward to the right, point P is on the y-axis and has coordinates (0,2), and O is the origin. From P, draw a perpendicular to this line, with foot Q; in the figure, OP is the vertical downward line segment from P to O, and PQ is the perpendicular segment from P pointing to Q. According to the problem statement, the slope of the line y = 1/2 x + b is 1/2, so the slope of PQ perpendicular to it is -2; therefore, a direction vector of PQ can be taken as (1,-2). The direction vector from P to O is PO = (0,-1), or a scalar multiple in the same direction. Using the two-dimensional vector angle sine formula, sin∠OPQ = |det((0,-1),(1,-2))| / (|(0,-1)| |(1,-2)|) = |0·(-2) - (-1)·1| / (1·√5) = 1/√5 = √5/5. The condition b < 2 only affects the position direction of Q in the figure and does not affect this sine value.
